name: Link Button
propertyCopy: Set the button’s size, content, corners and label.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview Link-type Button reads visually like a hyperlink - no box, no fill, just colored text - but behaves and is marked up as a button-style action rather than a real navigational link. It sits between Anchor (plain inline text for wayfinding) and a boxed button (a clear call to action). When to Use Navigation-style actions inside button groups or toolbars - View Details, Learn More, View All. Actions that feel like "going somewhere" rather than "doing something" - Go to Dashboard. Contexts where a boxed button would look too heavy but the action still needs to sit among other buttons - a card footer's row of actions. When Not to Use Plain inline text links inside a paragraph or list - use Anchor instead - it's built for exactly that case and is semantically a link, not a button. The primary action of a form or flow - use Primary - a Link-styled button under-communicates urgency. Irreversible or high-stakes actions - always use a boxed Destructive button so risk is visually obvious. Best Practices Reserve the Link type for actions living among other buttons, not for body copy - use Anchor there instead. Give it an underline on hover/focus so it still reads as interactive despite having no box. Avoid placing more than one Link-styled button in the same row as a Primary button - it can visually compete despite its low weight. Do and Don't Do Read the full changelog for details. Inline, inside a sentence, taking the reader somewhere - what a link is for. Don't Delete workspace A destructive action styled as a Link looks like the least important thing on the page, which is the opposite of what a high-consequence action should signal. Accessibility Still a real <button> element, not an <a> - screen readers announce it as a button, matching its actual behavior (no href, no navigation). Underline or color change on focus, never color alone, to signal keyboard focus. Text color meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast against the surrounding background in both themes.
